name: Katie Petit
fact: The archive carries Katie Petit in 2003-04 and Katie Pettit in 2005-06 and 2006-07, and they may be one person. The Herald spells her Pettit both times: Katharine Pettit ran for senate in March 2004 saying her freshman standing made her a good candidate, and the March 2005 section calls her Upton sophomore Katie Pettit. A freshman senator in 2003-04 fits the Petit entry exactly. Flagged, not merged: the portrait cut from that 2004 page is already published as Katie Pettit, so no face is filed for Katie Petit until the two entries are resolved.

name: Brooke Smith
checked: Every digitised College Heights Herald 2002-2009 was searched by its embedded text layer. Her name appears on exactly one page: 26 September 2002, p. 5, in the SGA budget-irregularities story, where she is named as one of the congress members who signed the petition that started the investigation.
why: She is named in text and never photographed. That single page carries no news photograph at all, only a Depo-Provera advertisement. No other frame of her exists in the digitised run.

name: Jonathan Sprowles

name: Josh Fries

why: The 10 April 2008 photograph is the closest thing to a frame of him and it is not him: the caption names only Chief Justice Brian Fisher (left) and leaves the two other justices in the frame unidentified, and Fries is the absent party whose tied election the council was discussing. name: College Heights Herald, August to December 2006
checked: data/herald-index-full.json holds 27 College Heights Herald issues for 2006 and every one of them is from January to May. The run stops at 4 May 2006 and picks up again on 23 January 2007. All 152 TopSCHOLAR items dated later in 2006 are annual reports, programmes, newsletters and oral histories.
why: This is why the 2006-07 executive is so thin in this block. Amanda B. Allen, Matt Holland, Emilee Bishop, Cacy Schooler, Jonathan Sprowles, Josh Fries, Lucas Humble, Tim Hill, Meggan Selzer and Andy Vandiver all took office in a semester the archive does not hold. The only route into it is wkuherald.com in the Wayback Machine, which has 112 archived article pages dated August to December 2006.

name: 2003 Talisman (About Face)
checked: The only Talisman published between 1994 and 2012 is the 2003 volume, UA12/2/2 About Face, dlsc_ua_records article 1594. It was pulled through the Wayback route, 158 pages at 1804 by 2378 pixels with a clean 277,000-character text layer, and every officer surname on this block was searched against it.
why: It is a documentary yearbook, not a portrait book. There are no class portrait grids and no student government section, and not one officer of 2002-03 is named in it. There is no Talisman at all for 2004 through 2011, so the yearbook route is closed for this entire block.

name: Spirit Masters Scrapbook 2005 (stu_org 1326)
checked: Pulled through the Wayback route, 24 pages at about 2,000 pixels square, no text layer, so every page was rendered and read with ocrmac. Pages 3 and 4 carry the whole 2004-05 class as individual portraits with name, class, major and hometown printed beside each.
why: Not one of the officers on this block is in that class. The names are Barnett, Burcham, Carman, Carter, Corum, Farrell, Manning, Lovan, Lebrand, Jones, Inman, Fausey, Hodson, Hale, Griffin, Whitfield, Martins, McFarland, McKinley, Peck, Petkova, Sutton, Stark, Raley, Ransdell, Smith, Shepherd, Roth and Rink. The format is worth remembering: these scrapbooks name and picture every member of a class, so 1320 (2002) and 1325 (2008) are live leads for other blocks.

kind: SOURCE FOUND: portraits with printed names
name: Spirit Master of the Month advertisements in the Herald
checked: WKU Spirit Masters bought a monthly advertisement in the Herald through these years. Each one prints one or two studio portraits with the person's name and month set directly beneath the frame. That is what gave this block its Natalie Croney portrait, from 17 February 2004 p. 5.
why: Recorded as a lead, not a dead end. Other months name Nichole Johnson (November 2002), Amber Braden (December 2002), Leslie Peek (October 2003) and Lindsey Ransdell (February 2004). The embedded text layer of these advertisements is unreliable, so they have to be found by eye or by OCR, not by grepping the PDF text.

kind: probable duplicate person, flagged not merged
name: Drew Eclov / M. Andrew Eclov
checked: The archive carries Drew Eclov as senator and chair of Academic Affairs in 2007-08 and M. Andrew Eclov as Director of Academic and Student Affairs in 2008-09, from SGA's own minutes of 16 October 2007 and 26 August 2008. The Herald calls him a Lexington freshman in March 2007, a Lexington sophomore in October 2007 and a Lexington senior in December 2010.
why: Almost certainly one man: Drew is the ordinary short form of Andrew, the surname appears nowhere else in the whole 2002-2010 Herald, the hometown matches and the career runs straight on from committee chair to director. The same 2010 mugshot is now filed under both names, as 2008-09-m-andrew-eclov.jpg and 2007-08-drew-eclov.jpg. Flagged rather than merged, because merging people is the editor's call, not a photograph agent's.
